To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a systematic approach for simulating NV that combines low level computer algorithms with high level human feedback to produce realistic NVs that are useful in the development of computer-aided detection systems.

(i) we developed an interactive system that enables ophthalmologists to guide the process of simulating NVs; (ii) we developed two algorithms that simulate the main structure and color of NVs; (iii) our method is able produce photorealistic lesions that can not be differentiated from real lesions by ophthalmologists; (iv) we demonstrated the potential of our method by using the simulated NVs to train an automated lesion detector.

we propose two novel algorithms to simulate neovascularization and an adaptive color assignment method to produce realistic color fundus images, which can be used to train and evaluate computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) algorithms for diabetic retinopathy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computer-aided system to support the simulation of NV in digital retinal images.
the development of a simulation tool to generate realistic lesions that can be used to train and validate computer-aided detection algorithms.
the development of an effective method to simulate NVs in color fundus images for computer-aided DR diagnosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the simulation method proposed in this work has the potential to provide a valuable resource for researchers and clinicians who are interested in developing and testing computer-aided detection methods of DR.

this paper proposes a systematic approach to simulate neovascularization in color digital retinal fundus images, which can be used to develop computer-aided detection algorithms for diabetic retinopathy.
our method is a valuable tool to support the development of NV detection algorithms.

we have developed a systematic method for simulating NVs in retinal images.
the proposed method is able to simulate NVs in color digital retina images that are indistinguishably realistic from real lesions.
our method is an important step toward the development of computer-aided detection of NV in retinal images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
computer simulation of NVs can serve as an alternative to collecting large numbers of real images to test and develop NV detection algorithms.
the proposed method is a promising approach for computer simulation of NV.
the simulation method can generate NVs that are realistic enough to be used in developing NV detection algorithms.
